A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 29-page versions of the same NSNQuant paper, including Appendices A–I. Pages 2–29 have identical extracted text and rendered content, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original NSNQuant benchmark, ablation, memory, throughput, and latency experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the additional benchmark evaluations and AIME-2024 experiment in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical NSN transformations, Hadamard processing, scale adjustment, codebook tuning, double quantization, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Coverage remains identical, including WikiText-2, C4, the LongBench subset, GSM8K, HumanEval, CoQA, MMLU, AIME-2024, and the synthetic efficiency scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including KIVI, KIVI + Hadamard, KVQuant, CQ, and the QuaRot and SpinQuant comparisons in Appendix F.6.

E3.justification: Both retain the same evaluation protocols, including 4096-token main perplexity evaluations, residual size 64, baseline controls, generation settings, and appendix experimental configurations.

E4.justification: The component ablations, residual-size sensitivity tests, scaling and codebook comparisons, normalization variants, CQ calibration-set experiments, and distribution analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain latency averaging over 100 runs in Section 4.6 and AIME-2024 evaluation with five seeds in Appendix F.5. Statistical and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted outcomes, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs, including the main benchmark tables and all appendix results.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and its assumptions, the proof in Appendix A, attention derivations in Appendix B, and normalization mathematics in Appendix D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about calibration-free quantization, generalization, low-bit performance, and throughput. The added code-access sentence does not revise these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distribution shift, benchmark noise, and latency tradeoffs remain unchanged. Appendix I retains the same limitations concerning early-layer outliers and inter-channel dependencies.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit NSNQuant GitHub repository link to the abstract; v2 supplies no corresponding code-access link. This improves documented access information, while implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix H's comparison with CQ, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or research-positioning arguments are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 appends one code-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All remaining wording, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual changes are confined to the first page: the code link occupies the existing final abstract line, and the updated arXiv margin stamp appears lower. All figures, tables, captions, and rendered pages 2–29 are identical.

improvement.justification: The newly supplied repository link provides a previously missing route to the implementation, modestly improving reproducibility information and usability. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.
